draft.full_post:
A solo Google engineer just pointed 48 autonomous AI agents at raw NASA LiDAR data.

In 72 hours, they found a completely unmapped Maya pyramid.

What usually takes archaeological teams years of machete-hacking through jungle terrain was solved over a weekend for practically zero marginal cost.

Here is why this matters for software teams:

⚡ 𝗦𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗺 𝗨𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆: It wasn't one massive model doing the heavy lifting, but a network of 48 focused agents cross-checking candidate coordinates.
🔍 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝗕𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗲-𝗙𝗼𝗿𝗰𝗲: Problems once gated by human attention spans are becoming trivial parallel compute tasks.
📌 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿'𝘀 𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲: One developer with an orchestrator now has the discovery bandwidth of an entire research department.

When brute-force analysis costs virtually nothing, what is the biggest backlog problem in your industry that is suddenly solvable?
